# Injective Morita Contexts and Morita α-Contexts: An Exposition

## Introduction and Scope

This paper provides a comprehensive exposition of two important classes of Morita-theoretic structures. The first class consists of **injective Morita contexts**, which are characterized by the property that their connecting bimodule morphisms are injective. The second class comprises **Morita α-contexts**, in which the connecting bimodules exhibit local projectivity in the sense of Zimmermann-Huisgen. By focusing on these refined structures, we aim to clarify the interplay between injectivity of the connecting maps and projectivity properties of the underlying bimodules, both of which play a central role in the theory of module category equivalences.

## New Structural Notions: Semi-Contexts and Morita Data

A significant contribution of this work is the introduction of two new notions: **Morita semi-contexts** and **Morita data**. These concepts arise naturally from situations that fall outside the scope of the classical Morita context framework. Specifically, Morita semi-contexts are motivated by settings in which only a single trace ideal is available, rather than the pair of trace ideals typically required in the classical theory. Morita data, on the other hand, address situations in which the connecting bimodule morphisms lack the compatibility conditions that are usually imposed. By relaxing these requirements, these new notions extend the reach of Morita theory to a broader range of algebraic contexts and provide a unified language for treating asymmetric or partially compatible structures.

## Equivalences via Injective Morita Data

Building on these foundations, we employ injective Morita data—together with the classes of **static** and **adstatic modules**—to establish category equivalences. The central results characterize equivalences between certain intersecting subcategories, which are formed from modules that are either localized or colocalized by the relevant trace ideals. The use of static and adstatic modules is essential here, as these classes precisely capture the objects on which the natural transformations associated with the Morita data become isomorphisms. This approach yields a transparent description of the equivalences and clarifies how the trace ideals govern the localization and colocalization processes that determine the relevant subcategories.

## Applications

The paper concludes by demonstrating the utility of Morita α-contexts through several applications. First, we apply these structures to the study of **∗-modules**, a class of modules of considerable importance in representation theory and the theory of tilting. Second, we explore connections to **injective right wide Morita contexts**, showing how the framework developed here illuminates their structure. These applications underscore the versatility of Morita α-contexts and confirm that the local projectivity conditions at their core have meaningful consequences across a variety of module-theoretic settings.

# Injective Morita Contexts, Semi-Contexts, and Generalized Morita Theory

## Introduction

Classical Morita theory provides a powerful framework for understanding when two rings share equivalent module categories. At the heart of this theory lies the notion of a Morita context, a structure that encodes the interplay between two rings through a pair of bimodules and a pair of bilinear pairings. When these pairings are surjective, the associated rings are Morita equivalent, and their module categories are indistinguishable up to equivalence. However, many situations of interest arise where such strong surjectivity conditions fail, motivating the search for weaker structures that still yield meaningful category-theoretic correspondences.

This paper investigates injective Morita contexts and Morita α-contexts, with the aim of extending the reach of classical Morita theory to broader and more flexible settings. To accomplish this, we introduce two novel notions: **Morita semi-contexts** and **Morita data**. These constructions systematically relax the requirements imposed on ordinary Morita contexts. In particular, they dispense with certain compatibility conditions between the bimodule morphisms, and they allow one to work with only a single trace ideal rather than requiring both trace ideals to be present and to interact in a prescribed manner. By loosening these constraints, we obtain a versatile machinery capable of handling a wider class of examples than the classical theory admits.

## Framework and Main Results

A central theme of our analysis is the role played by **static** and **adstatic modules**. These modules are precisely those for which the natural evaluation and coevaluation maps arising from the context behave optimally, and they form the appropriate domain on which category equivalences can be constructed. Rather than seeking an equivalence between entire module categories—which is generally unavailable in the absence of surjective pairings—we localize and colocalize the relevant categories with respect to the trace ideals determined by the context.

Our principal results establish category equivalences between suitably intersecting subcategories. Specifically, the subcategories obtained by localizing or colocalizing at the trace ideals, when intersected with the classes of static and adstatic modules, are shown to be equivalent. This refinement captures the essential content of Morita-type correspondences in a setting where global equivalences need not exist, and it clarifies exactly which modules participate in the equivalence and how the trace ideals govern this participation.

## Applications

The theoretical framework developed here yields concrete applications in two directions. First, we apply our results to **∗-modules**, a class of modules that has attracted considerable attention because of its close connection to tilting theory and its role in generalizing progenerators. Our approach sheds new light on the categorical behavior of ∗-modules by situating them within the language of Morita semi-contexts and data.

Second, we treat **injective right wide Morita contexts**, demonstrating how the injectivity hypotheses interact with the relaxed structural assumptions to produce well-behaved equivalences. These applications illustrate the explanatory power of our constructions and confirm that the generalized notions are not merely formal abstractions but genuinely useful tools.

## Conclusion

By introducing Morita semi-contexts and Morita data, and by analyzing them through the lens of static and adstatic modules, this work extends classical Morita theory into a substantially more general landscape. The resulting category equivalences between localized and colocalized subcategories provide a unified perspective that encompasses injective Morita contexts, Morita α-contexts, ∗-modules, and injective right wide Morita contexts, thereby enriching our understanding of the deep relationship between rings, modules, and the equivalences that connect them.

# Abstract

**Injective Morita Contexts and Morita α-Contexts**

In this paper, we investigate the structural properties of injective Morita contexts and introduce the notion of Morita α-contexts as a natural generalization. A Morita context $(R, S, M, N, \phi, \psi)$ is said to be *injective* when both of its associated pairings $\phi: M \otimes_S N \to R$ and $\psi: N \otimes_R M \to S$ are injective maps. We establish that injectivity of a Morita context is equivalent to several module-theoretic conditions and demonstrate how this property is preserved under standard constructions, including matrix ring formations and localization.

We then define a *Morita α-context* by weakening the injectivity requirement through a compatibility parameter $\alpha$, allowing the pairings to admit prescribed kernels controlled by an ideal or a preradical. This framework unifies and extends classical results connecting Morita theory with the transfer of ring-theoretic and homological properties between $R$ and $S$. In particular, we show that for a Morita α-context, key invariants—such as primeness, semiprimeness, and various radical properties—are transferred between the two rings in a manner governed by $\alpha$.

Our main results characterize when the trace ideals generated by the images of $\phi$ and $\psi$ inherit the injectivity structure, and we provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which a Morita α-context reduces to an injective Morita context. As applications, we recover known Morita invariance theorems as special cases and derive new criteria for the equivalence of module categories associated with α-contexts. Several examples and counterexamples are presented to illustrate the sharpness of the hypotheses and to delineate the boundaries of the theory.

---

*Keywords:* Morita context, injective Morita context, Morita α-context, trace ideal, Morita invariant, ring homomorphism, prime radical.

*2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:* 16D90, 16S50, 16D20, 16N60.

# Abstract

**On Morita Contexts, Locally Projective Modules, and Trace-Induced Category Equivalences**

We develop a unified framework generalizing classical Morita theory by relaxing the requirement of a strictly surjective pairing in a Morita context to conditions governed by trace ideals and local projectivity. Given a Morita context $(R, S, {}_R M_S, {}_S N_R, \varphi, \psi)$ in which the connecting bimodule homomorphisms need not be surjective, we characterize the resulting category equivalences between subcategories of $R\text{-Mod}$ and $S\text{-Mod}$ determined by the trace ideals $T_R = \varphi(M \otimes_S N)$ and $T_S = \psi(N \otimes_R M)$. Central to our approach is the notion of local projectivity in the sense of Zimmermann-Huisgen: a module ${}_R M$ is locally projective precisely when every finite subset lifts through epimorphisms in a manner compatible with the $\alpha$-condition, a strictly weaker hypothesis than projectivity that nonetheless suffices to control the behavior of trace ideals under the relevant tensor and Hom functors.

Our principal results establish that when ${}_R M$ is locally projective and the associated pairing is nondegenerate, the functors $N \otimes_R -$ and $\mathrm{Hom}_R(M, -)$ restrict to inverse equivalences between the trace-torsion-free quotient categories, generalizing the Morita I, II, and III theorems to this non-unital, non-surjective setting. We further show that the trace ideal $T_R$ is idempotent and that the category of $T_R$-divisible, $T_R$-torsionfree $R$-modules is equivalent to a corresponding category of $S$-modules, thereby recovering the theory of equivalences induced by idempotent ideals and rings with local units as special cases. As applications, we characterize when a locally projective generator induces such an equivalence, relate our constructions to the *-modules and tilting-type contexts of Colpi–Trlifaj, and provide criteria under which local projectivity can replace full projectivity in the classification of self-generators. Examples arising from infinite-dimensional algebras, semiperfect rings, and comodule categories illustrate the necessity of the local projectivity hypothesis and the sharpness of our trace-theoretic conditions.

**Keywords:** Morita context, trace ideal, locally projective module, category equivalence, idempotent ideal, $\alpha$-condition, self-generator.

**MSC (2020):** 16D90, 16S50, 16D40, 18E10.
